newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks close slightly up as golds soar.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks close slightly up as golds soar.

text.p: Australian shares closed slightly firmer on Friday, with gold stocks rebounding after this week's heavy sell-off. But the market finished the week weaker due to the precious metal's continuing woes.
The All Ordinaries index was 4.7 points up at 2,699.1, but off its morning high of 2,703.7. Trade was brisk with A$730 million (US$540 million) worth of shares traded.
Traders said the market steadied in afternoon trade as local investors took positions ahead of Friday's U.S. June Producer Price Index, which may set the tone for Wall Street.

Brokers said there were buying opportunities in local gold stocks, which had dropped more than 20 percent during the week to Friday morning after the bullion price slipped around five percent on last week's news of the Australian central bank's 167-tonne gold sale.
"You would definitely have to say they (gold stocks) have found support," said Tim Phillips, investment director at Tyndall Investment Management.
Brokers said the positive gold sentiment was felt in the rest of the resource sector, which ended positively, while the broader industrial sector eased.

Shares in beverage group Coca-Cola Amatil went for a rollercoaster ride, falling 50 cents earlier, but ending the day just 12 cents down on concerns that the Philippine peso's woes may affect its recent exposure to the Philippine market.
Brokers said there was not much impact on the market from the 8.4 percent fall in May's housing finance figures.
Financial markets had been braced for a monetary easing this morning following Thursday's weaks job data, but no move was made.

ICI Australia shares eased ahead of the announcement of its final price bid price from the sell down by its former parent ICI Plc. Tyndall's Phillps said he expected investors to pay A$12.40 for the ICI shares.
